paragraphs: Early in the morning, reach a disabled machine at a worksite and read codes for a preliminary diagnosis. During the day, crawl under the chassis, inspect hydraulics, listen for unusual sounds, replace assemblies, and document work. In the afternoon, test and calibrate the machine before returning it to service. Scheduled-maintenance periods run continuously, and field lodging is routine.

In short: return disabled heavy equipment to service. Read codes, inspect hydraulics, replace assemblies, test, document, and maintain. The role combines judgment and hands-on skill as a worksite stabilizer.
